answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a beacon as the anchor of the cost.
